title: 💺 @Tuesday.Global is fair game
text:

Today, our warm capacity in the EU and AU is not very much used. However, we do have some workloads that have global residency: serving them anywhere is fair game. If these workloads can use that global capacity, while scaling up their regional capacity, this could save us money.

Goals - Send global workloads anywhere Constraints - Never violate data residency Feasibility and Impact - About 98% of US jobs are global (Nov 12 to 18). - Jobs: 98.1% of 8.36M US jobs with an org id are global. The other 1.9% (155k) are US resident and stay in the US. - Pages: 99.4% of 82.7M are global. - A US job is resident only when its org has an active us flag. 31 orgs (17 accounts) have the flag, and 14 of them sent jobs that week. - EU jobs are never global: every one is EU. AU sent 11k jobs. - Source: Tinybird job_analytics by org, joined with Snowflake CORE.ADMIN.DATA_RESIDENCY_ORGS. 1.48M more US jobs have no org id in that table. In a 16-hour sample, every one matched an org through analytics_events, and 5.6% belong to flagged orgs. With them the share is about 97.6%. - The share is only as good as the flags. Some contracts with a residency clause have no flag yet (sent to Jean, Nov 18). No lending before that list is clean. - Feasible for the EU now. The EU router holds warm Modal slots for 6 namespaces, almost all idle. AU has no router traffic and no controller, only the R-1 mini floor on Modal. - Tinybird, Nov 16 to 18 UTC, by minute. In use = router leases over warm slots. Movable = share of the US queue an idle EU slot could have taken. | Namespace | EU slots | EU in use | Minutes with a US queue | Avg US queue | Movable | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | maverick | 155 | 3.1% | 2.8% | 9.8 | 28% | | figsum | 198 | 2.0% | 5.4% | 3.0 | 75% | | fpp-35b | 97 | 1.2% | 3.8% | 22.0 | 16% | | extract-v4-magpie | 23 | 0.5% | 7.3% | 1.7 | 48% | | citation-7b | 12 | 0.3% | 11.1% | 1.7 | 32% | | fpp-2b | 92 | 0.2% | 2.2% | 3.6 | 26% | - In every minute with a US queue, the EU had at least one idle slot. - Movable assumes every US call is global. About 98% of US jobs are, so the real share is close. Step 2 counts it per namespace. - Residency: the worker marks a call global only when the job's resolved residency is GLOBAL and the job is not AU-restricted. Only such a call gets a cluster in another region. EU jobs are always EU, so no EU call leaves the EU. Metrics - Utilization in EU and AU - Number of calls that are served instead of waiting Questions - What share of US calls is global? Answered (Nov 18): about 98% of US jobs, 99.4% of pages (Feasibility). Step 2 still counts calls per namespace. US-flagged accounts on the US endpoint stay in the US. - How many EU slots can the US take? Answered (Jean, Nov 17): no fixed reserve; the EU controller sets the lend limit by feedback (step 4). - Is latency fine for a US worker calling EU Modal? The page image crosses the Atlantic twice. Step 2 measures it on staging before prod. - AU? Answered (Jean, Nov 17): out for now. Modal cannot place the 35B in AU. Decide again after the step 8 read, once AU R-1 mini is on the router. --- # Execution ## Plan - Step 1: router and R-1 calls know global ([PR 15234](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15234), merged) - A global_only cluster serves only global calls, and only when their region is full. - No call moves yet: no environment has such a cluster. - Step 2: count global calls and time the US to EU path - Counter per namespace, global or resident ([PR 15396](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15396), merged). Only R-1 calls send global today; the other five router callers send it with [PR 15397](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15397) (merged). - Time 100 R-1 pages from a US worker to EU staging Modal, against the same pages in the US. - Step 3: US calls borrow EU capacity as low-priority calls through the EU router (on top of [PR 15178](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15178)) - A lent call never queues: the EU router refuses it (429) when an EU call waits or the lend limit is reached. - Why the EU router: the EU is Modal only, and Modal's capacity answer has no calls in flight. Only an EU lease lets the EU cap count the US call. - A lent lease stays out of the Modal target, so it never adds an EU container. - PR 15178 allows low-priority calls on GPU clusters only; this PR extends it to Modal. - Step 4: EU lend limit set by feedback (same controller code as the low-priority limit) - One number per namespace. Starts at 0. - +1 each tick while no EU call waits and the EU has a free slot. - Halves when an EU call waits while a lent lease is live. router.lend_displaced counts each halving. - The key expires after 30 s, so a stopped controller stops lending. - Step 5: US router sends global calls to the EU router - The EU router is the US router's global_only cluster, capped at the lend limit the EU reports (US controller writes it with a 30 s expiry). - A refused call goes back to the US queue. The call span names the serving region. - Step 6: one Doppler key for the EU router in the US router Secret (Jean) - Nothing is on before this. - Step 7: turn it on per namespace (1 values PR each; Jean deploys all regional routers together) - fpp-35b first, the largest US queue. PostHog share 10, 25, 50, 100. - Then fpp-2b, maverick, figsum, magpie, citation. Each call site first passes global. - Step 8: read the metrics after one week - EU utilization (leases over slots), calls served on EU slots instead of waiting, US waited share, halvings. ## Logs - Nov 17, 6:05 PM PT: measured EU slots and the US queue (Feasibility). Step 1: [PR 15234](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15234) in review; Jean deploys the router, no config change. - Nov 17, 6:30 PM PT: wrote steps 2 to 8. No PR work on them until Jean stamps the plan. - Nov 18, 5:25 PM PT: measured the global share of US jobs: 98.1% of jobs, 99.4% of pages (Feasibility). - Nov 18, 5:30 PM PT: checked the residency flags against contracts, Salesforce and Attio. With the jobs that have no org id, the share is about 97.6%. Some accounts with a residency clause or a BAA have no flag. List sent to Jean. - Nov 18, 5:37 PM PT: step 1 merged ([PR 15234](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15234)). No call moves yet. - Nov 19, 2:54 AM PT: Jean stamped the plan. Every lending switch stays off until he settles the missing flags and what a BAA means. - Nov 19, 3:02 AM PT: step 2 counter opened ([PR 15396](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15396)). The timing is not run: EU staging has no R-1 in the EU, so Jean is choosing between an EU staging deploy and 100 pages on prod EU off-peak. - Nov 19, 3:14 AM PT: the other five router callers send global ([PR 15397](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15397)). No call moves. - Nov 19, 9:35 AM PT: both step 2 PRs merged ([PR 15396](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15396), [PR 15397](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15397)). The counter reports after the next router deploy. The timing still waits on Jean's choice. ## Impact - Baseline: 98.1% of US jobs (99.4% of pages) have no residency limit, so they can run in EU or AU. Measured on US prod jobs, Nov 12 to 18 (Jensen), reported 2026-11-18. - Before, EU warm slots in use (Tinybird, Nov 16 to 18 UTC): maverick 3.1% of 155, figsum 2.0% of 198, fpp-35b 1.2% of 97, extract-v4-magpie 0.5% of 23, citation-7b 0.3% of 12, fpp-2b 0.2% of 92. - Before, minutes with a US queue: 2.2% (fpp-2b) to 11.1% (citation-7b); the largest average queue is 22.0 calls (fpp-35b). In each of those minutes the EU had an idle slot. - After: no call moves yet. Step 1 ([PR 15234](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15234)) is merged and no environment has a global_only cluster. - First split of router admits (Datadog router.admit.global, [#15396](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15396), read 2026-11-19 15:00 PT). US prod, 10:18 to 15:00 PT Nov 19: 89% of 6.36M admits come from jobs with no residency rule (R-1 mini 99.5%, Citation 7B 99.0%, highlight detection 98.1%, R-1 96.6%, FigSum 96.2%, Qwen 95.2%, core CV 94.9%, Magpie 94.4%, change tracking 78.9%, Maverick 76.4%). EU prod (router deployed 14:57 PT): 1,183 admits in two minutes, none. Nothing is lent: no prod config has a cross-region cluster. - EU utilization, calls served on EU slots instead of waiting, US waited share and GPU cost per 1k pages: not measured yet; measure at step 8.
